# RFC requirements ledger

What this repository does about each MUST, SHOULD and MAY of the RFCs it implements, and which test says so. The rules are in `scripts/check_rfc_ledger.py`.

## JSON Web Signature (JWS), RFC 7515 (`rfc7515`)

GAP 2, IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED 24, NOT_APPLICABLE 19, NOT_SUPPORTED 8, PARTIAL 3, SUPPORTED 5, TESTED 8

| Section | Keyword | Status | Severity | Requirement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Header Parameter names must be unique; parsers must reject duplicate names or keep only the lexically last one. |
| 4 | MUST | PARTIAL | medium | Implementations must understand and process the spec-defined header parameters marked 'MUST be understood' (alg, crit). |
| 4 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Spec-defined header parameters not designated 'MUST be understood' must be ignored when not understood. |
| 4.1.1 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | alg must be present and must be understood and processed by implementations. |
| 4.1.11 | MUST | PARTIAL | medium | Extensions named in crit must be understood and processed; a JWS with an unsupported critical extension is invalid. |
| 4.1.11 | MUST | PARTIAL | medium | The crit header parameter must be understood and processed by implementations. |
| 5.2 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | At least one JWS Signature value must validate, or the JWS must be considered invalid. |
| 5.2 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | The algorithm must be accurately represented by the alg header value, which must be present. |
| 5.2 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | If none of the signature validations succeeded, the JWS must be considered invalid. |
| 5.2 | SHOULD | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Unless the algorithm is acceptable to the application, a JWS that validates should still be considered invalid. |
| 5.3 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | JSON string comparisons must use the RFC 7159 rules, except typ and cty values. |
| 6 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Key-identifying header parameters must be integrity protected when used in a trust decision. |
| 8 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Whenever TLS is used, the server certificate's identity must be verified per RFC 6125. |
| 10.6 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Where a library reads the hash from the signature, the encoded algorithm must be checked against alg. |
| 10.12 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | JSON inputs not conforming to RFC 7159 JSON-text must be rejected in their entirety. |
| 10.12 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Header Parameter names within the JOSE Header must be unique; parsers must reject duplicates or keep the lexically last. |
| 10.12 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Producers must treat RFC 7159's uniqueness SHOULD as a MUST; consumers reject duplicates or follow ECMAScript 5.1. |
| 4 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | low | Header parameters not defined by this specification must be ignored when not understood, unless listed in crit. |
| 4.1.4 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | low | A kid value must be a case-sensitive string. |
| 4.1.9 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | low | A recipient using a typ media type must treat a value with no '/' as if 'application/' were prepended. |
| 4.1.11 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | low | When used, crit must be integrity protected and so may occur only in the JWS Protected Header. |
| 5.2 | MUST NOT | GAP | low | In the JSON Serialization the same Header Parameter name must not occur in both the protected and unprotected headers. |
| 7.2.1 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | low | The signatures member of the general JSON Serialization must be an array of JSON objects. |
| 7.2.1 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | low | header must be present when the unprotected header is non-empty, and absent otherwise. |
| 7.2.1 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | low | Members of the signature objects that an implementation does not understand must be ignored. |
| 7.2.1 | MUST | GAP | low | The Header Parameter names in the protected and unprotected headers must be disjoint. |
| 8 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | low | Confidentiality protection must be applied using TLS with a ciphersuite giving confidentiality and integrity. |
| 10.12 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | low | A JWS whose JSON has extra significant characters after a valid value must be considered invalid. |
| 10.13 | SHOULD | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | low | JWS implementations should preserve and compare characters outside the BMP correctly, else reject input containing them. |

## JSON Web Token (JWT), RFC 7519 (`rfc7519`)

APPLICATION 1, DEVIATION 1, IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED 19, NOT_APPLICABLE 16, NOT_SUPPORTED 8, PARTIAL 3, SUPPORTED 1, TESTED 2

| Section | Keyword | Status | Severity | Requirement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4.1.1 | OPTIONAL | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | high | The iss claim is optional; when used it is a case-sensitive StringOrURI whose processing is application specific. |
| 4.1.3 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | high | Each principal intended to process the JWT must identify itself with a value in the audience claim. |
| 4.1.3 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | high | A JWT whose aud claim is present but does not contain the processing principal's identity must be rejected. |
| 4.1.4 | MUST NOT | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | high | A JWT must not be accepted on or after its exp time. |
| 4.1.4 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | high | Processing exp requires the current date/time to be before the expiration date/time in exp. |
| 7.2 | SHOULD | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | high | Unless the algorithms used are acceptable to the application, the JWT should be rejected even if it validates. |
| 4 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Claim Names must be unique; a parser must reject a JWT with duplicate Claim Names or keep only the lexically last. |
| 4.1.2 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | The subject must be locally unique in the issuer's context or globally unique; a consumer must not treat sub alone as identity. |
| 4.1.2 | OPTIONAL | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | The sub claim is optional; its processing is application specific and it is a case-sensitive StringOrURI. |
| 4.1.3 | MAY | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | With one audience the aud value may be a single case-sensitive string instead of an array. |
| 4.1.3 | OPTIONAL | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Use of the aud claim is optional. |
| 4.1.4 | MAY | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Implementers may allow a small clock-skew leeway, usually no more than a few minutes. |
| 4.1.4 | OPTIONAL | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Use of the exp claim is optional. |
| 4.1.5 | MUST NOT | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | A JWT must not be accepted for processing before its nbf time. |
| 4.1.5 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Processing nbf requires the current date/time to be after or equal to the nbf date/time. |
| 4.1.5 | MAY | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Implementers may allow a small clock-skew leeway for nbf, usually no more than a few minutes. |
| 5.1 | OPTIONAL | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Use of the typ header parameter is optional; any processing of typ is performed by the JWT application. |
| 7.3 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | The JSON string comparison rules of RFC 7159 section 8.3 must be used for all JSON string comparisons except typ and cty. |
| 4.1.4 | MUST | PARTIAL | low | The exp value must be a number containing a NumericDate value. |
| 4.1.5 | MUST | PARTIAL | low | The nbf value must be a number containing a NumericDate value. |
| 4.1.5 | OPTIONAL | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | low | Use of the nbf claim is optional. |
| 7.2 | MUST | PARTIAL | low | If any of the JWT validation steps fails, the JWT must be rejected (treated as invalid input). |
| 8 | MUST | DEVIATION | decided | Of the JWA signature/MAC algorithms only HS256 and 'none' must be implemented by conforming JWT implementations. |

## JSON Web Token Best Current Practices, RFC 8725 (BCP 225) (`rfc8725`)

APPLICATION 6, GAP 1, IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED 9, NOT_APPLICABLE 10, PARTIAL 6

| Section | Keyword | Status | Severity | Requirement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3.1 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | high | The library MUST ensure the alg/enc header names the same algorithm that is actually used for the cryptographic operation. |
| 3.2 | SHOULD NOT | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | high | JWT libraries SHOULD NOT consume JWTs using alg none unless the caller explicitly requests it. |
| 3.3 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | high | All cryptographic operations in a JWT MUST be validated, and the whole JWT MUST be rejected if any of them fails. |
| 3.8 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | high | If the keys do not belong to the issuer, the application MUST reject the JWT. |
| 3.9 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | high | The relying party MUST validate the audience, and MUST reject the JWT if aud is absent or not associated with the recipient. |
| 3.2 | SHOULD | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | A verifier SHOULD treat a JWS as invalid when its algorithm is not acceptable to the application, even if the signature verifies (RFC 7515 5.2). |
| 3.2 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Applications MUST only allow cryptographically current algorithms that meet the application's security requirements. |
| 3.5 | MUST NOT | PARTIAL | medium | Human-memorizable passwords MUST NOT be used directly as the key of a keyed-MAC algorithm such as HS256. |
| 3.7 | MUST | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Implementations MUST use UTF-8 for JSON in headers and claims, and not use or admit other Unicode encodings. |
| 3.10 | SHOULD | IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED | medium | Applications SHOULD protect against SSRF via jku/x5u headers, e.g. a URL allow-list and no cookies in the key fetch. |
| 3.1 | MUST | PARTIAL | low | A library MUST let the caller specify the supported algorithm set and MUST NOT use any other algorithm for cryptographic operations. |
| 3.1 | MUST | PARTIAL | low | Each key MUST be used with exactly one algorithm, and this MUST be checked when the cryptographic operation is performed. |
| 3.2 | MUST | PARTIAL | low | Applications MUST be designed to enable cryptographic agility, so algorithms can change as they weaken. |
| 3.2 | SHOULD | GAP | low | JWT libraries SHOULD implement ECDSA using the deterministic approach of RFC 6979. |
| 3.5 | MUST | PARTIAL | low | The key-entropy and random-value advice of RFC 7515 10.1 and the password considerations of RFC 7518 8.8 MUST be followed. |
| 3.8 | MUST | PARTIAL | low | When a JWT has an iss claim, the application MUST validate that the keys used for its cryptographic operations belong to that issuer. |
